page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with numbered paragraphs (18–21) that open with an indent. No marginal notes. Running head at the top. Page number at the top right.

main_text.p: nasteria, vel Hieronymo teste, vt controuersiæ 5. lib.2.oftendimus. tum posteriorum seculorum monasteria sanctimoniæ priorum respondere, aut respondisse iamdiu: postremo optimos, sapientissimos, vtilissimos fuisse Pontifices qui ex illis lacunis emerserunt, quæ hodie Ecclesiam & mundum totum inficiunt fœtore suo.

18 Ibid. Monachus certè fuerat S. Dionysius.] æ-quinoce:nam aliud est Monachus secessum quaerès extra ordinem vt persecutiones fugiat & Deo seruiat, aliud ex voto ordinariam faciens monasticen & necessariam: illos qui fuerunt olim, laudamus, hos, qui fingunt sibi monasteria ad meritum, improbarnus. non fuit Dionysius de isto genere.

19 Ib. Monachus fuerat S. Gregorius, id est, pietatis & literarum sacrarum studiosus, quibus & se & alios in secessu informaret. Atq; hi Monachi tū nō erat de clero, vt ipse Bellarmin agnouit aliquoties controuersia 5. finaute[?] ad clerū promoti efsét, Monachi & Clerici siue Monachi & Leuitę dicebätur, vt Gregorie appellat Platina. Eadè Adeodati & Agathonis, & aliorū ratio, qui minore superstitione, maiore sanctimonia & studio exercuerunt monasticen, sed ab ista otiosa & superstitiosa plurimum dissidete, quę posteà in peius ruit cū ipso seculo. Nō ita sunt monachi huius seculi, qui has laudes veterū iustas ne per somnium quidem cogitant decerpere. Non sequitur quicquā ex particulari, & diuerso tempore.
20 Ibid. satis eum contra venenatas detractorum linguas communiebant.] de hoc Gregorio dictum satis controuersiæ 3.lib.4.cap.13.
21 Ibid. vt ipsòfe Pontificatu sponte abdicauerit.] de hoc Celestino videndum supra cap.14. Sed quid tā multis opus est? Monachos veteres meliores fuisse

page.notes: Printed "nasteria" at the top is a fragment of "monasteria" carried over from the previous page. "finaute" is doubtful. "quinoce" may carry a tilde over the e. "tā" is an abbreviation for "tam", read with doubt. "improbarnus" appears as printed (likely a printing error for "improbamus"). Paragraph numbers 18–21 are part of the text and are kept as printed.
